## Reuters confirms Samsung wins $200B Broadcom AI chip partnership, boosting foundry ambitions

Reuters confirmation of Samsung winning Broadcom's AI chip manufacturing business is a tangible foundry win that could narrow the perceived quality gap with TSMC; for AVGO holders, it signals a credible dual-source fabrication strategy that may reduce execution risk on the custom ASIC roadmap.

- Reuters has confirmed that Samsung Electronics secured a $200 billion AI chip manufacturing partnership with Broadcom, upgrading earlier cluster coverage to confirmed status.
- The deal is characterized as a boost to Samsung's foundry business, which has been competing to close the gap with TSMC for advanced AI chip workloads.
- Reuters and The Economic Times coverage gives the confirmation high credibility with institutional audiences.
- Samsung is positioned as Broadcom's preferred AI chip fabrication partner — a relationship with multi-year strategic implications for the foundry competitive landscape.
